newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak dismisses Khartoum's peace partners.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak dismisses Khartoum's peace partners.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak dismissed the Khartoum government's new peace partners on Thursday as "small tribes" and said the peace agreement was a device to help Khartoum out of its troubles.
Five small factions signed the agreement on Monday, but not the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang, the mainstream rebel movement in the south.
"The Sudanese opposition has not agreed with him (Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir), no," Mubarak told army officers at a military ceremony in the town of Suez.

"They brought some of those small tribes and got them to agree but the opposition -- the Umma Party, the Unionists and Garang and all that group -- are still there. He's looking for something to break the deadlock," Mubarak added. His remarks were broadcast on state television.
"Of course our aim is that Sudan should be an ordinary state, not one that shelters terrorist camps," he said.
Egypt says that the Islamist government in Khartoum sheltered the gunmen who tried to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995 and that it has supplied weapons to Egypt's own Islamists.
